{"Author":"Zeffuro, Pie Lover","Name":"AetherBags","Punchline":"Never think too hard about your bags again!","Description":"This plugin replaces your inventory with it's own categorified inventory addon.","Changelog":"Adds a fast symbol picker letting you quickly insert any symbols into supported in-game text fields.
It is designed to make commonly used symbols easier to access without manually copying them from third-parties or typing them every time.

## Features
- Adds a floating quick-access "♥" button for opening the symbol popup
  - Allows the "♥" button position to be changed through drag-and-drop repositioning
  - Provides a symbol popup for quickly selecting and inserting symbols
  - List shows ALL existing custom symbols for FFXIV
- Supports opening the symbol popup through a configurable keybind
- Ensures only one symbol popup is open at a time
- Allows keybind-opened popups to be temporarily moved by dragging empty space inside the popup
- Includes a character selector toggle option for symbol selection behavior
- Adds an optional "Close popup on lost focus" setting to auto-close the popup when clicking outside of it
- Adds quick popup controls for closing the popup, changing the "♥" button position and opening the config window
- Includes a help tooltip explaining how to properly use some features

## Notes
The plugin is intended as a lightweight quality-of-life tool for players who frequently use special symbols in chat, search fields, notes or others","TestingChangelog":"# 1.0.0.5
- Added the ability to hide/show game categories in the Category Configuration.
- Added the ability to hide/show external/built-in categories in the Category Configuration.
- Fixed a crash that can occur when closing the Changelog window.
- Fixed a crash that could occur opening the housing menu.

{"Author":"NetStyx","Name":"A Realm Repopulated","Punchline":"The realm, now with more realm in it","Description":"This plugin aims to give players the ability to add more flavor npcs to the common areas of the game.","Changelog":"# 0.1.8.0 Changelog

Reworks the scenario editor, lets actors sprint or move at a custom speed, open automatic doors, and makes following the player character with their head more reliable.

## Functional Changes
- UI Rework of the scenario editor
- Actors can now sprint, or move at a custom speed, with their steps matched to it
- Automatic doors now open and close for actors
- Reworked the changelog tab into a release list with the selected release's notes beside it

## Technical Changes
- Following the player character with the head no longer hooks into the game, so it is less likely to break on game updates

## Bugfixes
- Fixed actors sometimes not following the player character with their head, or not looking away when the player character left quickly
- Fixed the path preview in the editor disappearing when the camera faced away from part of the path
- Fixed scenarios getting stuck or no longer looping when actors had a different number of Sync actions, an actor's last Sync action was disabled, a path started where the actor already stood, or a Timeline action had no timeline selected
- Fixed actors stopping just short of the last point of a path
- Fixed actors being left behind frozen when a scenario could not be fully loaded, or when a scenario was changed on the title screen or during a loading screen
- Fixed a possible crash when a scenario was reloaded right after its actors appeared","TestingChangelog":"# 0.1.8.0 Changelog

{"Author":"Bronya Rand","Name":"Things To Do In Eorzea","Punchline":"Unsure what to do? Forgot what you wanted to do? Nonsense! There's always things to do in Eorzea!","Description":"
Keep track of all your objectives and tasks in Eorzea. Whether it's collecting tomes/items/gear, completing dungeons/trials/raids, FATEs, or purely making a random list of things to do to keep yourself busy, keep yourself organized and on track with this plugin.

Features:
    - Create and manage a list of objectives and tasks.
    - Automatically track your progress on objectives and tasks.
    - View your objectives and tasks with a window inspired by the in-game Duty Log.
    - Automatic translation of objectives and tasks to your game client's language. (No need to write what you want to do. Just setup how you want to do it and the plugin will fill in the rest!)
    - Open creativity for just about anything that comes up to mine! (...What? You don't think making silly challenges like doing Endsinger's Aria - Extreme with MINE in under 12 minutes a good idea? Seriously, you can make that a task if you want)
       
Inspired by the idea of "DYOM" (Design Your Own Mission) and "TTDISA" (Things To Do In San Andreas) from GTA: San Andreas as well as Simple To-Do List and other similar plugins.
    ","Changelog":"**XivReflex** integrates [NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency](<https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/reflex-low-latency-platform/>) to reduce system input lag in GPU-bound scenarios by dynamically aligning the game's engine updates closer to the moment your GPU actually draws the frame on screen.

**Requirements:**

- NVIDIA GeForce 900 Series or newer
- NVIDIA Driver version 456.38 or newer","TestingChangelog":"Things To Do In Eorzea is more than just a simple to-do-list. It's one that automatically monitors what you need to collect, what duties you need to clear, FATEs and more! You can either set it up to track items you need or have it track your clears. Think that's not enough? You can even set yourself up some ridiculous tasks for yourself like doing MINE Bahamut or a whole Savage round without dying/wiping to just simply forcing yourself to play a specific job, or speedrun. There are always things to do in Eorzea. Just get creative!

Unlike other to-do plugins, Things To Do In Eorzea:
1. Auto-tracks your completed dungeons, trials and raids.
2. Auto-tracks your completed FATEs by region, a specific FATE or any FATE in general.
3. Auto-tracks the items in your inventory, making sure you have what you needed to get.
4. Make self-imposed challenges like doing Minstrel's Ballads on MINE difficulty, speedrun a Dungeon, one-shot/no kill, and more.
5. Read objectives in your native language*

   > French is partially broken ATM pending a Dalamud merge.

And you still have your sticky note for whenever you need it.

AI Use: Assist
> AI was used to inquire about translations from English to Japanese to show there was at least an attempt to show that localization is supported. However said translations may not be accurate. Anyone interested may PR or DM me their translated findings for German, Japanese and French if they so please. Thus far:
> - Full English on UI and Objective Display
> - Full Japanese [Claude+Gemini+Google Translate+DeepL+Japanese Dictionary] on UI and Objective Display
> - German only on the Objective Display with partial assistance from XIV community for macros and Claude
> - French only on the Objective DIsplay with assistance from Gemini and Clause
> 
> There was also AI assist for the localization system.","Tags":["to-do,list,track,task,objective,custom,utility,ui,other"],"CategoryTags":["utility","ui","other"],"IsHide":true,"InternalName":"ThingsToDoInEorzea","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.0.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"1.0.0.0","IsTestingExclusive":true,"RepoUrl":"https://github.com/Bronya-Rand/ThingsToDoInEorzea.git","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"DownloadCount":489,"LastUpdate":1787607241,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://kamori.goats.dev/Plugin/Download/ThingsToDoInEorzea?isUpdate=False&isTesting=False&branch=api9&isDip17=True","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goatcorp/DalamudPlugins/api9/plugins/ThingsToDoInEorzea/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://kamori.goats.dev/Plugin/Download/ThingsToDoInEorzea?isUpdate=False&isTesting=True&branch=api9&isDip17=True","LoadPriority":0,"ImageUrls":null,"IconUrl":null,"AcceptsFeedback":true,"FeedbackMessage":null,"FeedbackWebhook":null,"_isDip17Plugin":true,"_Dip17Channel":"testing-live"}

- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value
  /bocchi buff → Start/stop a buff run
  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE
  /bocchi reload-translations → Reload translation files (alias: rt)
  /och … → Same as /bocchi (legacy alias; also /occultcrescenthelper)

{"Author":"Faye, Kage","Name":"Better Occult Crescent & Chest Helper Interface","InternalName":"BOCCHI","Punchline":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.","Description":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.
- No more of that pesky 'walking' or 'finding chests'. That's for losers.
- A cute little Fate and CE panel that'll tell you what rewards it gives AND help you automatically path to it, wowee.
- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys

{"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","Punchline":"Automatically accept or decline Duty Finder ready checks based on a configurable counter.","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

- **Treasure**: takes the best choice instead of only suggesting it. Live button clicks confirmed choice *k* is event param `2+k`, so the pick path that was already built can fire.

v0.1.1.0 (2026-09-21)

- **Beast Feed**: picks the familiar each feed helps most in the fights ahead and confirms it (kin, satiety, no repeats, knocked-out familiars honoured).
- **Shop**: buys the heals, resistances, gear and feed the upcoming fights call for; never sells and never leaves the shop.
- **Spoils**: takes everything when it all fits; otherwise lists the best items first.
- **Campsite**: selects which familiars rest; Rest stays with the player.
- **Treasure**: marks the best choice and explains why.
- **Fight guide** (`/lazycrucible guide`): all five boards, with horn picks and their reasons, dangerous hits, mechanics and what to bring; opens on the next fight.
- **Hands back**: any input made by hand on one of these screens, or AutoDuty running, hands that screen back to the player. Each screen has its own switch, on by default.
- **Error reporting** covers the new screens: a screen automation that keeps failing drops the input in flight, pauses with one chat notice and retries on its own.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-21)

- **First release**, split out of GluttonyCombo: the Beastmaster familiar selection for Crucible of the Unbroken now lives here, and GluttonyCombo keeps the Beastmaster rotation. Both automations are on by default and each has its own switch.
- **Run roster**: on the Bentbranch Meadows entry menu, sets the ten familiars that cover the board's battles best, once per visit.
- **Battlehorns**: on the formation screen before every fight, puts the three familiars that answer that fight's mechanics on the horns (elemental weakness, interrupts, dispels, cleanses, crowd control the enemies are vulnerable to). Knocked-out familiars are never picked; badly hurt ones lose to a healthy familiar that fits nearly as well. The fight itself is never started.
- **Picks in chat**: one line per fight naming each familiar and why it was chosen (`"Announce picks in chat"`). The window shows the latest selection.
- **Manual edits win**: a roster or horn change made by hand (or by another tool) stops the automation for that screen, and a roster edited that way is kept for the rest of that visit.
- **Stands down for AutoDuty**: while AutoDuty is running a board (it picks its own familiar team), the familiar screens are left alone (`"Stand down while AutoDuty is running"`, on by default).
- **Fixed** (carried over from GluttonyCombo testing builds): the item shop's Beast Feed screen was treated as the Battlehorn screen, so feeding a familiar after the elite fight could fail or move the feed target. The feeding and campsite screens are now never touched.
- **Fixed** (carried over): a run roster cleared and rebuilt on the entry menu (by hand or by AutoDuty) is no longer overwritten mid-edit.
- **Beast-pick advisor**: picks for every battle on every board, the board roster and familiars worth capturing, under "Beast picks by battle".
- **Screen recorder** (`"Record Crucible screens to the log"`, read-only): writes each Crucible screen and every button pressed on it to the Dalamud log, groundwork for automating the path, spoils, treasure, shop, feeding, campsite and beast gear screens.
- Stands down with a chat notice while a GluttonyCombo version that still fills familiars itself is loaded.
- **Problem reports**: `/lazycrucible report <what happened>` or the "Report a problem" button writes a report to the plugin log with the zone, job, recent familiar-selection and screen lines, and the full contents of the Crucible screens that are open.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyRetainerLive","Punchline":"Real-time retainer venture countdowns for your dashboard.","Description":"Serves the logged-in character's live retainer and venture state on loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1:10504) so the ffxiv dashboard relay can show real-time venture countdowns instead of AutoRetainer's occasionally-stale file cache.","InternalName":"LazyRetainerLive","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.1","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.1","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"Changelog":"v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)

That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. - For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.

- Why this exists: AutoRetainer's `DefaultConfig.json` (which feeds the dashboard today) is saved only at AutoRetainer's own save points, so its venture rows can be tens of minutes stale while ventures are actually completing.
